description.narrative:
The CPF III will contribute to the realization of the Child Protection programme outcome that seeks to ensure that: by 2026, children, adolescents and young people are better protected from violence, abuse and exploitation, are registered in a timely manner and benefit from improved prevention and response systems in development and humanitarian settings.
Access to child protection and welfare services including birth registration for the most vulnerable children through the National Case Management System
Prevention of VAC and GBV through interventions that address harmful practices, social and gender norms and behavioural drivers of violence.
Access to child-friendly justice system and services
Policy, legal and regulatory framework improvements and reform, coordination and institutional capacity strengthening

The main purpose of CPF III is to contribute to the UNICEF Country Programme Document (CPD) 2022- 2026 which is aimed at contributing to sustainable socioeconomic development that provides all children, including adolescents, with opportunities to fulfill their potential, lead a healthy life, access quality learning and protection and meaningfully participate in society is to strengthen and maintain the functionality of the child protection system especially in the face of limited fiscal resources from the State. In particular the CPF III will contribute to the realization of the Child Protection programme outcome that seeks to ensure that: by 2026, children, adolescents and young people are better protected from violence, abuse and exploitation, are registered in a timely manner and benefit from improved prevention and response systems in development and humanitarian settings.
In order to achieve this outcome, realise this vision, the CPF III project will provide support across four Result Areas. These are described below.
Result Area 1. Access to child protection and welfare services including birth registration for the most vulnerable children through the National Case Management System. UNICEF will support protection and welfare response interventions to address violence against girls, boys and women in 10 high priority CP districts. It will also ensure that all children and adolescents, including those most vulnerable, have access to birth registration services.
Result area 2. Prevention of VAC and GBV through interventions that address harmful practices, social and gender norms and behavioural drivers of violence. The focus of this result area is to ensure that: Communities, caregivers, children, adolescents and young people have the information, knowledge and skills that address harmful social and gender norms, promote positive care giving and early detection and response of protection risks.
Result area 3. Access to child-friendly justice system and services
Under this result area, UNICEF will support the Government to implement its child-related justice delivery commitments, through strengthening of relevant institutions, decentralizing institutions for justice delivery including the Legal Aid Directorate and the courts, improving access to justice for vulnerable people including women, children and persons with disabilities, aligning laws to the Constitution, and establishing integrated electronic case management system, among others.
Result area 4. Policy, legal and regulatory framework improvements and reform, coordination and institutional capacity strengthening.
The focus of this result area is to ensure that: An effective child protection and GBV legal, regulatory and policy framework is in place to prevent and respond to child protection and GBV risks, and institutional capacity to enforce it.

Programme results in 2025 were strong across prevention, service delivery, and justice outcomes. At the systems level, CPF III advanced key reforms, including operationalisation of the Persons with Disabilities Act, development of the National Disability Identification and Referral Framework, and rollout of the National Ending Violence Against Children Roadmap, strengthening coordination and inclusion. Evidence generated during the year showed that cultural and religious systems can act as protective factors against child marriage, while nearly 90% of children with disabilities were found to be affected by climate shocks, shaping more targeted and resilient programming.
At community level, CPF III exceeded prevention targets, reaching 2,624 adolescents, 2,164 caregivers, 1,378 community childcare workers, and 1,205 traditional and religious leaders. Parenting interventions contributed to reductions in violent discipline, while disability-inclusive programming trained 748 caregivers of children with disabilities, enabling 352 children to access integrated services. Community ownership drove additional outcomes, including traditional leaders enforcing restrictions on harmful practices linked to child marriage. However, 7,691 adolescent girls accessed child marriage services, highlighting persistent and widespread vulnerabilities, particularly in hotspot districts.
Service delivery results also surpassed expectations. A total of 17,842 children (against a target of 15,000) accessed services through the National Case Management System, contributing to over 51,747 children reached nationally. Strengthened case management improved early identification, referral, and follow-up, with community-based social workers extending services to underserved areas. Birth registration coverage for children under five increased to 57%, exceeding the 52% target, with more than 55,000 children reached through mobile, digital, and solar-powered registration services. District outreach demonstrated strong uptake, with Makonde registering 364 individuals and Binga issuing over 300 birth certificates, 86% of which were for children under five. However, findings also revealed large numbers of older unregistered children and continued reliance on fee waivers, reflecting persistent financial and access barriers. A case involving 18 undocumented migrant children in Harare further highlighted emerging cross-border protection risks.
Child-friendly justice systems showed significant progress, with 99% of children in conflict with the law diverted from custodial sentences toward non-custodial, rehabilitative measures. Capacity building reached 587 justice actors, and 8,788 survivors of violence, including 2,636 children, accessed services through Victim Friendly Systems, exceeding targets. Decentralisation improved access to justice but also exposed previously unmet demand, alongside emerging challenges such as online exploitation, cross-border cases, and complex family situations.
Overall, 2025 results demonstrate that CPF III systems are delivering at scale and exceeding targets, but also reveal persistent structural gaps, rising demand, and evolving risks. Continued constraints including limited fiscal space, declining external funding, weak subnational capacity, and the fact that an estimated 43% of children remain unregistered underscore the need for sustained investment to consolidate gains and ensure equitable access to child protection services.
